tenders.title: Design, Installation, Maintenance and Support of Electronic Security Systems
tenders.summary: Given the evolving threat environment both in Canada and internationally, NRCan is focused on strengthening the physical security posture of its facilities.
tenders.text: design, installation, maintenance and support of electronic security systems given the evolving threat environment both in canada and internationally, nrcan is focused on strengthening the physical security posture of its facilities. this includes improving access control, surveillance, and intrusion detection capabilities to ensure personnel safety and operational continuity. nrcan operates an electronic security and surveillance system consisting of access control, video management, and intrusion detection systems deployed across multiple locations nationwide. the system is maintained through a combination of in-house it and security resources, as well as contracted security system support and integration services. the system transitioned from legacy analog infrastructure to an ip-based architecture between 2016 and 2020, with ongoing enhancements through 2023. the current security system is built on a hybrid cloud and on-premises architecture, designed to balance cost and performance with confidentiality, integrity, and availability requirements. the system includes approximately 500 card readers and 500 cameras across more than 25 sites and is monitored through the nrcan security operations control centre (socc) located at 580 booth street in ottawa, ontario.

tenders.text: purchase of eleven (11) electrometer/high-resistance meters and accessories (keithley 6517b or equivalent) the national research council canada (nrc) requires to purchase eleven (11) electrometer/high-resistance meters and accessories (keithley 6517b, or equivalent). the equipment is used continuously in applications where low-current and high-resistance measurements require exceptional signal-to-noise performance, stability, leakage control, guarding, triaxial connectivity, and measurement repeatability. metro operates under a rigorous quality system and maintains measurement standards that must be demonstrably traceable, reliable, and internationally recognized. the existing keithley-based measurement platform has been fully integrated into validated measurement systems, software applications, automation scripts, operating procedures, and technical documentation. maintaining the same instrument platform supports compatibility with internationally accepted metrology practices and helps ensure continuity and comparability of measurement results used to support national measurement standards and regulatory obligations. the use of an equivalent manufacturer's instrument would require extensive technical evaluation and verification before it could be incorporated into operational measurement systems. this work would include performance testing, comparison studies, revalidation of measurement methods, review and potential revisions, updates to quality-system documentation, modifications to software drivers and automation scripts, and assessment of impacts on established laboratory pro

tenders.text: acan-nrcan nuvis techonologies inc. support the petawawa research forest (prf) is a 10,000-hectare (ha) research forest located in chalk river, ontario. the land, which the prf is on, is owned by the canadian department of national defence (dnd), garrison petawawa, however, under a joint memorandum of understanding (mou) the prf is staffed and operated by natural resources canada (nrcan). under this mou, nrcan is responsible for wildfire detection for the entire property, approximately 30,000 ha’s. to date, fire detection on the property has been conducted using two fire towers with cupola’s (27.5 and 38.5 metres tall) staffed with personnel who visually detect fires/smoke and biangulate the location. in 2018, the 38.5-metre-tall tower was decommissioned limiting our ability to detect fire on the property. there is also a radio tower located on prf property. this tower, referred to as the “radio tower”, has not been used for fire detection in the past. however, this tower has electrical power, which supplies power to the radio repeater that is currently on the radio tower. the radio tower can have more than one piece of equipment attached to its structure (i.e. the radio repeater will remain on the radio tower) and is a suitable location for a fire detection camera. nrcan was able to replace the existing fire detection system in 2022 by way of installing two optical camera sensor systems with fire detection monitoring software by nuvis technologies inc. the objective of this requirement is to renew hardware and softwar

tenders.title: Collection of surface water samples and ancillary data for the Canadian Water Monitoring Program for Pesticides in priority Ontario watersheds.
tenders.summary: Health Canada (HC) evaluates the risks to human health and the environment associated with the use of pesticides and regulates pesticide products in Canada under the Pest Control Products Act.
tenders.text: collection of surface water samples and ancillary data for the canadian water monitoring program for pesticides in priority ontario watersheds. health canada (hc) evaluates the risks to human health and the environment associated with the use of pesticides and regulates pesticide products in canada under the pest control products act. in the interest of increasing the availability of real-world data for use in pesticide risk assessments, hc coordinates the canadian water monitoring program for pesticides (cwmpp). as part of this program, water samples are analysed to determine the concentrations of pesticides present in canadian waters. federal laboratories will analyse approximately 200 chemicals (i.e., pesticide active ingredients and transformation products) in water from various regions across canada. ancillary data and expert advice assist in improving our collective understanding of any patterns observed or any potential levels of concern. october 26, 2026: added q&as.

tenders.summary: The work consists of the furnishing of all plant, labour, equipment and material for material disposal at Codroy, NL. In general, work under this contract will consist of, but will not necessarily be limited to, the following: 1.
tenders.text: material disposal - codroy nl the work consists of the furnishing of all plant, labour, equipment and material for material disposal at codroy, nl. in general, work under this contract will consist of, but will not necessarily be limited to, the following: 1. removal of previously excavated/dredged material, which is currently stockpiled at the sch main site in codroy, nl. the disposal location for the soil is the dfo breakwater site northwest of the main facility. note that the existing stockpile contains remnants of a plastic/enviroliner in amongst the soil. there may also be some wood and other debris in amongst the stockpile, from the previous dredging operations. in all cases, the plastics, wood, etc., are to be removed prior to disposing of the soil at the disposal site. plastics/wood/etc., removed from the stockpile is to be transported off site and disposed of at a provincially approved waste disposal facility. 2. supply and installation of class “b” and class “a” granulars. 3. supply and installation of 300mm diameter rock fill capping material to cover the soil at the disposal site. 4. supply and installation of stone barricades at the approach to the disposal area.

tenders.summary: The Canadian Space Agency (CSA) is recognized worldwide for its support to the exploration of space. An example of this support is the CSA’s contribution of the OSIRIS-REx Laser Altimeter (OLA) instrument to the asteroid sample return mission OSIRIS-REx.
tenders.text: osiris-rex lab organic and inorganic analyses monitoring the canadian space agency (csa) is recognized worldwide for its support to the exploration of space. an example of this support is the csa’s contribution of the osiris-rex laser altimeter (ola) instrument to the asteroid sample return mission osiris-rex. osiris-rex is a nasa-led mission that returned a sample from asteroid bennu to earth in september 2023. in return for canada’s contribution of ola, canada will receive 4% by mass of the returned sample, marking canada’s first samples returned from another solar system body and the 5th country in the world to have samples collected in space. the csa is now expanding its laboratory capacity to prepare for the arrival of its portion of the osiris-rex sample. specifically, csa seeks to monitor particulate and air contamination in its laboratories this analysis must be comparable to nasa and jaxa, who also monitor contamination in their curation facilities using vpd-icp-ms and td-gd-ms analysis of silicon wafers and absorbent tubes. accordingly, the canadian space agency requires a specialized service for monitoring organic and inorganic contamination in laboratories and clean rooms for the curation of astromaterials. the work will involve the following: 1. analysis of silicon wafers by vapour phase decomposition (vpd) inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (icp-ms) for trace metals; 2. analysis of silicon wafers by thermal desorption gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (td-gc-ms) for organic compounds; and 3. determination

tenders.title: Research Project on Service Navigation Support for Seniors
tenders.buyer: Department of Employment and Social Development (ESDC)
tenders.summary: Title: Research Project on Service Navigation Support for Seniors - 100032783 The Service Navigation Support for Seniors project will have two components.
tenders.text: research project on service navigation support for seniors title: research project on service navigation support for seniors - 100032783 the service navigation support for seniors project will have two components. the first component, component a will review the accessibility of information on support services available to seniors and/or their caregivers across all federal, provincial and territorial (fpt) jurisdictions and to identify common barriers. the objective of component a is to understand what support services are the most frequently requested across the 14 fpt jurisdictions and why the access rate for information is more elevated, especially as it relates to barriers in accessing them. the second component, component b, will use the results from component a and identify, in collaboration with fpt officials a number of case studies to analyse the mechanisms through which seniors and/or their caregivers learn about and/or access support services aiming to build awareness and improve access to service navigation supports. this would also include policy recommendations for jurisdictions to consider in enhancing service navigation support for seniors.

tenders.summary: Please return offers by email to solicitation-demandedesoumission@cnsc-ccsn.gc.ca Canada is seeking offers from qualified Offerors to provide professional services to review if and how thermal risk assessments (TRAs) are being conducted across the electrical…
tenders.text: thermal releases: review of international regulatory practices and options for incorporation into a compliance and licensing framework. please return offers by email to solicitation-demandedesoumission@cnsc-ccsn.gc.ca canada is seeking offers from qualified offerors to provide professional services to review if and how thermal risk assessments (tras) are being conducted across the electrical power generation industry domestically and internationally, and if there are any existing regulatory frameworks addressing management of thermal effluent. the work will identify gaps in the standardized application of tra methods and provide recommendations where applicable for improvement in standardization of tras for the nuclear power plants in canada. the scope includes a critical evaluation of thermal effects literature for reliability and relevance for being able to inform a tra, and the generation of an updated database of thermal effects thresholds for canadian relevant species fish, and invertebrate species in the marine and freshwater environment. the scope of this project also includes reviewing and compiling data on regulatory approaches used by different facilities utilizing once-through cooling system technology (e.g., nuclear power plants, oil and gas plants, etc.), nationally and internationally, with respect to thermal risk assessment and the derivation and application of thermal thresholds.

tenders.title: Wheel Force Transducers and Unmanned Ground Vehicle
tenders.summary: The Department of National Research Council Canada has a requirement for the supply of: 2.1.
tenders.text: wheel force transducers and unmanned ground vehicle the department of national research council canada has a requirement for the supply of: 2.1. four (4) wheel force transducers (wfts), acquisition modules, and accompanying hardware the wheel force transducers are required by the nrc to conduct terrain sensing and vehicle mobility research in arctic environments. 2.2. one (1) unmanned ground vehicle (ugv) for offroad robotics research the required ugv will function as a configurable research platform for the development, integration, validation, and demonstration of technologies including autonomous navigation, localization and mapping, perception, sensor fusion, path planning, mobility in complex and unstructured environments, human-machine teaming, remote operations, edge computing, and other physical artificial intelligence and field robotics applications. the end result of this procurement will be the delivery of a complete, operational, research-ready ugv platform that can be integrated into the existing technology ecosystem developed and maintained by the connected and autonomous vehicles (cav) team of the nrc. this procurement has been set-aside under the federal government's procurement strategy for indigenous business (psib). only indigenous businesses as defined under psib are eligible to challenge the proposed procurement strategy to award the contract to the named indigenous business.

tenders.title: Purchase of two (2) Millimetre-Wave Frequency Extender Modules for a Vector Network Analyzers (VNAs) from 110 GHz to 170 GHz
tenders.summary: NRC Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics (HAA) requires extended measurement capabilities in the millimetre-wave frequency range to support ongoing research in characterizing front-end components for low-noise receivers in radio astronomy.
tenders.text: purchase of two (2) millimetre-wave frequency extender modules for a vector network analyzers (vnas) from 110 ghz to 170 ghz nrc herzberg astronomy and astrophysics (haa) requires extended measurement capabilities in the millimetre-wave frequency range to support ongoing research in characterizing front-end components for low-noise receivers in radio astronomy. existing vector network analyzers (vnas) at nrc haa are currently limited to a maximum operational frequency of 116 ghz. to increase its measurement capability, nrc haa intends to acquire frequency extender modules covering the 110–170 ghz band. these extenders must integrate with either of haa's existing analysers (keysight pna n5227b and rohde & schwarz zna67), providing high dynamic range and stable two-port measurements.

tenders.title: Real Time Spectrum Analyzer
tenders.where: United States of America, South America, Central America, Caribbean, Asia, Africa, Europe, Mexico
tenders.summary: The National Research Council Canada has a requirement for the supply of a 1.2 GHz acquisition bandwidth real-time spectrum analyzer (26.5 GHz) to capture and stream in-phase and quadrature (I/Q) data.
tenders.text: real time spectrum analyzer the national research council canada has a requirement for the supply of a 1.2 ghz acquisition bandwidth real-time spectrum analyzer (26.5 ghz) to capture and stream in-phase and quadrature (i/q) data. the real-time spectrum analyzer will be used in a reverberation chamber to qualify duts against very stringent telescope protection levels. to achieve this, a low-noise, ultra-sensitive real-time spectrum analyzer is required. the real-time spectrum analyzer will capture and stream i/q data that is used to reconstruct complex time domain signals that are then transformed to the frequency domain where radio astronomy techniques of spectral integration are used to reduce the standard deviation of the noise.

tenders.text: enabling technology for future missions space technology development program background the space technology development program (stdp) mandate is to formulate, implement and manage contracted out research and development (r&d) projects in response to identified needs. its objectives are to develop and demonstrate strategic technologies that have a strong potential for reducing technical uncertainties for future canadian space activities. the stdp will therefore support the development of technologies to meet the current and future needs of the canadian space program. objectives the objective of this statement of work (sow) is to enable the development of space technologies that are in line with the canadian space agency’s (csa) priorities and mission roadmaps. for the priority technology (pt) specified herein (see appendix a-5 of annex a), the work solicited is the development and advancement of the technology (technology readiness levels (trl)), (see appendix a-1 of annex a) to reduce technical uncertainties and support approval and implementation of specific potential future space missions of interest to canada.

tenders.summary: The National Research Council on behalf of the Government of Canada (GoC) and its’ Partners seek to procure a secure, scalable, bilingual web-based digital platform (“the platform”) to support the reporting, review, analysis, and visualization of embodied…
tenders.text: web-based platform for whole building life cycle analysis (wblca) and embodied carbon emissions in building and infrastructure construction the national research council on behalf of the government of canada (goc) and its’ partners seek to procure a secure, scalable, bilingual web-based digital platform (“the platform”) to support the reporting, review, analysis, and visualization of embodied carbon emissions in building and infrastructure construction projects. this procurement includes the design, development, configuration, deployment and ongoing support of the platform. the solution will provide a centralized system that ensure consistent data collection, automated validation, and reporting in alignment with embodied carbon disclosure and reduction policies for buildings and infrastructure projects. at a minimum, the platform shall enable: - intake of material and project specific embodied carbon submissions; - import and export capabilities for compatible whole building life cycle assessment (wblca) submission reports and raw data; - dashboards and customizable reporting functions for internal analysis; and - the creation of an anonymized public dataset. the platform must comply with government of canada security requirements for protected a information and meet canadian-based data residency requirements.

tenders.text: e6hal-230008 pilot project for indigenous artists public services and procurement canada (pspc) has launched a pilot project to compile a list of emerging, mid-career, and established professional indigenous artists in the atlantic region. the list will be shared within federal departments and agencies in atlantic canada so that employees can use the list to procure indigenous art for use in government of canada buildings and offices in new brunswick, newfoundland and labrador, nova scotia, and prince edward island. this opportunity is open to emerging, mid-career, or established indigenous artists and artisans who create art or traditional crafts representative of the indigenous peoples in atlantic canada. to submit the required information for this opportunity complete the indigenous artist form at the following link: https://forms-formulaires.alpha.canada.ca/en/id/cmc1xkjh8001ex601pjp4kwcj once received, we will follow up to confirm if you are eligible. please be advised that inclusion on the list is not a guarantee that your business will be contacted to provide services. for questions or comments, please contact mailto:pwgsc.basatlantic-scaatlantiquetpsgc@tpsgc-pwgsc.gc.ca

tenders.summary: 1. Background The Department of National Defence (DND) moves materiel domestically and internationally on an as required basis to support operations and exercises.

tenders.title: Critical Incident Vehicles (CIVs)
tenders.buyer: Department of Public Works and Government Services (PSPC)
tenders.summary: The Government of Canada is seeking to establish Supply Arrangements (SAs) to procure: Critical Incident Vehicles (CIVs) in three (3) different Cab Chassis configurations Single Axle 4x2 or 4x4 or Tandem 6x4, equipped from a variety of specialized bodies for…
tenders.text: critical incident vehicles (civs) the government of canada is seeking to establish supply arrangements (sas) to procure: critical incident vehicles (civs) in three (3) different cab chassis configurations single axle 4x2 or 4x4 or tandem 6x4, equipped from a variety of specialized bodies for the rcmp. sas will be awarded to suppliers that meet all technical criteria and can provide all cab chassis and bodies configurations. offerors are encouraged to submit an indigenous participation plan (ipp) at the rfp stage as describe herein. an sa is a non-binding arrangement between canada and a pre-qualified supplier that allows departments and agencies to award contracts and solicit bids from a pool of pre-qualified suppliers for specific requirements within the scope of the sa. an sa is not a contract for the provision of goods and services described in it and neither party is legally bound, as a result of signing a supply arrangement alone. the intent of a supply arrangement is to establish a framework to permit expeditious processing of individual bid solicitations, which result in legally binding contracts for the goods and services described in those bid solicitations.

tenders.text: rfsa - provision of hydrographic/bathymetric production services. notice of proposed procurement (npp) this bid solicitation cancels and supersedes previous bid solicitation number 30004518 dated august 29, 2024 with a closing of october 16, 2025 at 14:00 atlantic time. submissions for 30004518 will no longer be accepted. this solicitation will remain on canadabuys until june 30, 2029. the canadian hydrographic service (chs) of fisheries and oceans canada (dfo) has a requirement to establish a number of supply arrangement (sa) with pre-qualified suppliers to meet the general requirements specified in each of the following service streams: a. stream 1: hydrographic/bathymetric training services; b. stream 2: hydrographic navigational charting support and production services; c. stream 3: bathymetric data assessment and processing services; and d. stream 4: hydrographic/bathymetric consulting services. these services will be required on an as required basis throughout the period(s) of the supply arrangement. the canadian hydrographic service (chs) is mandated to chart canadian waters to ensure safe navigation and to protect canadian sovereignty. in that endeavour chs must collect hydrographic/bathymetric data in support of new digital charting products as well as maintain existing portfolios of nautical charts in a variety of formats. this must be done using current international charting standards of data collection, processing and production. the proposed period of the supply arrangement is five (5) years from the date of issuance to decemb

tenders.summary: The Immigration and Refugee Board of Canada (IRB) is Canada's largest independent administrative tribunal. It is responsible for making well-reasoned decisions on immigration and refugee matters, efficiently, fairly and in accordance with the law.
tenders.text: immigration and refugee board of canada - interpreter program the immigration and refugee board of canada (irb) is canada's largest independent administrative tribunal. it is responsible for making well-reasoned decisions on immigration and refugee matters, efficiently, fairly and in accordance with the law. the irb decides, among other responsibilities, who needs refugee protection among the thousands of claimants who come to canada annually. every year, the board renders thousands of decisions on refugee protection and immigration matters. at these hearings, refugees and immigrants who are not fluent in english or french count on the irb to provide them with interpretive services. these interpretive services are required in a wide variety of languages and dialects, reflecting the diverse backgrounds of the refugees and immigrants who come to canada. in order to manage the interpretive services required for such a large number of hearings, including urgent hearings, irb issues contracts to interpreters who provide services on an “as-and-when-requested” basis and invoice for any services they provide. all interpreters are paid the same flat hourly rate. these contracts effectively work as a “roster” of potential interpreters who could be called upon to provide interpretive services at a hearing. selection for contract award: when selecting an applicant for a contract, the irb will consider several factors including the following: • the fluctuation of language demand with respect to immigration trends from specific regions. • previous in
